title: Lazur vs Willow Voice on Mac: fast AI dictation or a screen-aware assistant
metaTitle: Lazur vs Willow Voice on Mac: dictation or screen help?
description: Lazur vs Willow Voice for Mac, compared on price, privacy, platforms and features. Willow runs on Mac, Windows and iPhone. Lazur also sees your screen.
intro: Willow Voice is an AI dictation app, and Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates. Pick Willow if you mostly type by voice and need Windows or iPhone. Pick Lazur if you want spoken help with what is on your Mac screen. This page compares price, privacy, platforms and features using each company's own pages.
tldr: Willow Voice is a dictation app. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Willow covers Mac, Windows and iPhone. Lazur runs on macOS only, and Windows is planned.
Lazur sees your screen, points at buttons and answers out loud. Willow's site does not describe that.
Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial, then $18/month. Willow's Pro plan shows $12 per user per month on its pricing page.

blocks.text: The difference in one sentence

Willow makes typing by voice fast and tidy. Lazur makes getting help with your Mac fast, and it types too. Both start the same way: you speak, and text appears. They split after that, when you need an answer, a pointer or a step.
What Willow Voice does on a Mac

Willow Voice is AI dictation. You put the cursor in any text field, hold a hotkey, speak, and the text is inserted. It removes filler words and fixes punctuation. The homepage lists smart formatting, an auto-learning dictionary, shortcuts for phrases, 100+ languages and Whisper mode for quiet or noisy speech. A companion product, Willow Scribe, turns rough spoken descriptions into polished writing.
What Lazur does on a Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch on your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur dictates too. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. It also has snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Everyday jobs work by voice as well: timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts.
How well does each one dictate?

Willow's homepage claims 3x the accuracy of built-in dictation, with text appearing in as little as 200ms. Those are company claims, and this page does not test them. Product Hunt shows 4.8 out of 5 from 13 reviews. G2 shows 4.4 out of 5 from 28 reviews. Reviewers praise accuracy and ease of use. Product Hunt also says fast dictation sometimes turns non-English speech into English.
This page found no third-party ratings for Lazur, so it makes no rating claim. Judge both on your own work. Dictate the same paragraph in each app, then count the fixes you make afterward.
Where Willow Voice is the better pick

items: You need Windows or iPhone too. Willow lists Mac, Windows and iPhone. Lazur runs on macOS only, and Windows is planned, not available.
You want an offline mode. Willow advertises one, described as powered entirely by your device. Check its help center for which Macs and plans include it.
You dictate in many languages. Willow lists 100+ languages. Lazur's listed features do not give a language count, so test your language before you buy.
You want a free plan to start. Willow's Free plan is $0, and it needs no credit card. Lazur's only free period is its 3-day trial.
Your team needs admin controls. Willow's Business and Enterprise plans add admin controls. Enterprise adds SSO/SAML and API access.

blocks.text: Where Lazur is the better pick

items: You get stuck in apps. Ask Lazur to walk you through it. Lazur circles the button and waits for each click.
You want to ask what something on screen means. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask out loud. Lazur answers out loud and points at the part you mean.
You want everyday tasks by voice. Timers, Reminders, Calendar events, music and volume, and opening apps are built in.
You want research done in the background. Lazur runs research in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and returns a summary and a report.

blocks.text: Can you use Lazur and Willow Voice together?

Yes, if their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur dictates while you hold fn, and it asks while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Check Willow's shortcut settings for overlaps with those keys. G2 reviewers report shortcut conflicts in design apps such as Photoshop.
A worked example: one client reply, two apps

Say you reply to a client in Mail. The text reads: Maria, the invoice is $1,240 and due Friday. In Willow, you hold the hotkey, speak, and get that sentence with punctuation fixed. Willow's homepage says its dictionary learns on its own, so check whether names stick after a few sessions.

In Lazur, you hold fn in Mail and speak the same reply. The text lands at the cursor. If you forget the due date, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the invoice line says on screen. Lazur answers out loud, so you stay in the email.
Lazur vs Willow Voice pricing and plans

Lazur's pricing page lists a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. After that, Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

Willow's pricing page lists Free at $0, Pro at $12 per user per month, Business at $28 per month and Enterprise at custom pricing. Pro and Business show struck-through prices of $15 and $35. The page says Pro is per user, but it does not say whether Business is per user. Annual billing on Pro is labeled Save 20%.

blocks.text: Willow's prices do not match across sources. The App Store lists Pro Monthly at $15.00 and an annual plan at $143.99. A third-party review reports $15 per month and $144 per year. Confirm the rate at checkout before you assume $12.

The free word limit is unclear too. Willow's pricing page has a word limit row with no number in it. A third-party review reports 2,000 words per week on the free tier. Treat that as a claim until you see it in the app.

blocks.title: Test the trial on real work
blocks.text: Use the 3-day trial on a normal day. Dictate one email, ask one question about a window on screen, and set one timer. Those three jobs show where each app fits you.
Privacy: what each app keeps and sends

Lazur says it listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer you. Lazur says they are not stored, and that content is never used to train AI models. What you asked and did stays in memory on your Mac.

Willow's privacy policy, last updated August 5, 2026, makes Private Mode the default. Willow says that in this mode it does not retain dictated text or screen content. Voice audio is processed transiently and not kept. Its help center says transcript history stays only on the device. Context Awareness is optional and reads relevant text from the active window for transcription.

Willow's claims do not line up everywhere. The homepage describes zero data retention in broad terms. The help center lists enforced zero data retention only for Enterprise. The privacy policy names no specific subprocessors, only categories such as cloud infrastructure and transcription. The App Store privacy label is declared by the developer and not verified by Apple. It says usage and advertising data are linked to users for ads and analytics.

blocks.title: Ask which plan you are on
blocks.text: Willow's Business plan lists enforced privacy mode on its pricing page. The help center ties enforced zero data retention to Enterprise. If retention matters for your work, ask Willow in writing which plan includes it before you dictate sensitive material.
Which Macs and devices each one runs on

Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. Willow lists Mac, Windows and iPhone on its homepage. Android is not on that list. A third-party review lists Android, which conflicts with Willow's own list and with Product Hunt's note of no Android support. Treat Android as unavailable unless Willow confirms it.

Willow's iPhone app is a separate App Store listing. It shows version 2.13.2, requires iOS 18.0 or later and has an average rating of 4.6 from about 1.1K ratings. A Product Hunt reviewer says the iOS version forces you to switch apps. This page did not verify Willow's Mac or Windows version numbers.
The numbers that exist for dictation speed

The only primary study used here tested phone text entry, not Willow or Lazur. Ruan and colleagues found speech averaged 153 words per minute, against 52 for a QWERTY keyboard in English. That is about 2.93 times faster. Corrected errors during entry were 5.30% for speech and 11.22% for the keyboard. Uncorrected errors in final text were higher for speech, at 1.30% against 0.79%.

Read that as background, not proof. It says nothing about a Mac dictation tool. Measure your own speed with the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test), then time one real dictation in each app.
Mistakes people make when they compare these two

items: Judging dictation on one short sentence. Test a paragraph with names, numbers and a product term, then count the fixes.
Reading $12 as your bill. Check the monthly or annual choice and the App Store price before you subscribe.
Expecting Lazur to act for you. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It guides you one step at a time.
Skipping the privacy plan check. Confirm which Willow plan you are on before you dictate sensitive work.
Ignoring shortcut overlaps. Set each shortcut once and test it in the app you use most.

blocks.text: What to do next

items: Write down your two main jobs. If both are typing, Willow may be enough.
Install Lazur from the [download page](/download) and start the 3-day trial.
Ask Lazur to walk you through one feature you have never used. Watch it wait for each click.
Dictate the same paragraph into Willow's free plan and compare the fixes.
Keep the app that saved the most time, then check its plan before you pay.

blocks.text: Want the free built-in option first? Read [Lazur vs Apple Dictation on Mac](/compare/lazur-vs-apple-dictation). For Willow alternatives, see [Willow voice alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/willow-voice).

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Willow Voice alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in Mac apps and also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you one click at a time. If you need Windows or iPhone, or you only dictate, Willow Voice is the better fit.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Willow Voice together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur dictates while you hold fn and asks while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Check Willow's shortcut settings first, since G2 reviewers report conflicts in design apps such as Photoshop.

faq.question: Does Willow Voice work offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Willow's homepage lists an offline mode, described as powered entirely by your device. This page could not confirm which Macs or plans include it. Check Willow's help center before you rely on offline use.

faq.question: Which costs less, Lazur or Willow Voice?
faq.answer: Lazur Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually. Willow's pricing page shows Pro at $12 per user per month, struck through from $15, and a Free plan at $0. Lazur's only free period is its 3-day trial. Check each pricing page before you buy, since billing terms differ.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Willow Voice lists Windows on its platform list.

faq.question: Do Lazur or Willow Voice train AI on my dictation?
faq.answer: Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. Willow's privacy policy says Private Mode data is not used for model training. Its Help Improve Willow option is opt-in, and it may keep anonymized recognized text but not audio.

faq.question: Does Lazur type for me?
faq.answer: Lazur dictates clean text at the cursor when you hold fn. It guides you through clicks one at a time, but it does not click buttons or operate apps for you.
